Subject: Thanks for the demo — next steps / POC scope

Marissa —

Thanks for the demo today. Pete and I walked through Redwood’s latency/cost slides and the model routing examples; overall very interesting. We’d like to move forward with a short POC to validate two things for our production risk committee:

1) Inference economics on our typical query mix (retail banking conversational flows + document extraction)
2) Latency and availability under realistic traffic (spiky peak-hours)

High-level ask: can you send a proposed evaluation plan that includes success criteria, timeline, ownership, and any infra/credentials we’ll need to provide? Our target is to present to the risk committee on Aug 6; ideally the POC would finish by Jul 31 so we have time to summarize results.

Also looping in procurement (procurement@finservcorp.com) — they’ll want an outline of what we’ll need for temporary access and any trial terms.

Thanks — look forward to the POC outline.

John Patel
VP, Product
FinServCorp
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

John — thanks for the clear ask and for the time yesterday. Attached is a short POC outline designed to hit your two validation points and meet your committee timeline. Summary below; full outline attached (redwood-poc-outline.pdf).

POC objective
- Validate inference economics and latency/availability for FinServCorp conversational and extraction workloads.

Success criteria (proposed)
- Cost: < 0.20 USD per 1k tokens served for the evaluated workload (measured across 7-day sample)
- Latency: median request latency < 180ms and 95th percentile < 450ms for the conversational path
- Reliability: 99.5% availability during the test window; graceful fallback to a lower-cost model variant when autoscaling limits are hit
- Functional: end-to-end extraction accuracy within 5% of current baseline on the provided sample set

Evaluation plan / timeline
- Week 0 (Jul 16–18): Access + environment setup — we provision a temporary, isolated Redwood workspace for FinServCorp and request a 7-day sample of production traces + sample documents
- Week 1 (Jul 19–25): Run mixed load tests and extraction jobs; collect cost, latency, and quality metrics
- Buffer (Jul 26–28): Run any tuning/quantization suggestions; re-run limited tests if needed
- Results & deck (by Jul 31): Redwood delivers results, cost breakdown, and recommended next steps for production rollout; you present to risk committee on Aug 6

Ownership
- Redwood: Marissa (project sponsor) + Michael (SE lead) — provisioning, test harness, dashboards, model variants
- FinServCorp: John (product owner) + Lisa (data/sample owner) — provide traces, sample documents, and procurement contact for trial terms

What we need from you this week
- A 7-day sample of typical prod request traces (anonymized is fine) and 200 sample documents for extraction accuracy checks
- Procurement contact or PO process for trial access (procurement@finservcorp.com OK)

Attachments
- redwood-poc-outline.pdf (attached) — includes test harness details, network/credential checklist, and temporary SLA summary
- redwood-sla-summary.pdf (attached) — short summary of trial SLA and data handling commitments

If that looks good, we’ll kick off with a short setup call (30 min) with Michael to walk provisioning and credentials. I’m available Thu 7/16 at 10am PT or Fri 7/17 at 9am PT.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0127

John / Marissa — quick technical notes to make the setup smooth: 

- For the traces: please include request and response latencies, typical sequence lengths, tokenization settings (if custom), and any retry/backoff behavior in the client — that helps us pick batching/quantization profiles.
- For extraction accuracy: include the ground-truth labels/expected outputs for the 200 sample docs (CSV or JSONL is fine).
- Networking: we can support either (A) temporary API-key-based access from your staging CIDR ranges or (B) client-side TLS + signed JWTs for short-lived tokens. Option A is fastest for a 2-week trial.
- Data handling: Redwood will not persist raw document text beyond the trial window unless you opt in; logs and metrics are retained per the attached SLA summary.

I’ll provision the test harness and a Grafana dashboard for the metrics once we have the traces. Suggested setup call times OK for me — prefer Thu 7/16 10am PT.

-Michael
